title: Execution of the full carry phase
statement: Let $x$ be a finite binary input word, let $p$ be a valid input-head position for $x$, and let $b$ and $u$ be finite binary words. For every prefix $a$ of $b$, if the four-state binary-counter machine starts in state $1$ with input-head position $p$, work-head position $|a|$, the tape containing the concatenation of $a$ and $b$, and empty output, then after exactly one more step than the number of leading $1$ bits of $b$, it is in state $2$ with input-head position $p$, work-head position $|a|$ plus the number of leading $1$ bits of $b$ minus one, the tape containing the concatenation of $a$ and the increment of $b$, and empty output.
hypotheses_covered: $x$ is a finite binary input word
$p$ is a valid input-head position for $x$
$u$ is a finite binary word (unused in the conclusion)
the claim holds for every prefix $a$
replaced:
Suppose the four-state binary-counter machine is in its carry state with the
concatenation of binary words $p$ and $b$ on the nonnegative work-tape cells,
work head at cell $|p|$, and empty output, and let $r$ be the carry length of
$b$ (its number of leading $1$ bits). Then after exactly $r + 1$ steps the
machine is in the rewind state with the work tape holding $p$ followed by the
incremented word of $b$, the work head at cell $|p| + r - 1$, and the input
head and output unchanged.
